item.title: API
item.description: REST APIs These are reference contracts for your configured PMS/ADS or asserter endpoint. speedle.io serves documentation and the browser Playground; it is not a hosted PMS/ADS service. Supply JSON with Content-Type: application/json, and configure TLS/mTLS and caller access controls. Policy management API Authorization decision API Token assertion webhook Policy and role-policy IDs are strings. PMS responses are flat objects; authorization permissions use permissions (plural). REST decision requests use a typed attribute array, whereas diagnostic response attributes and webhook attributes are objects.

item.title: Authorization Decisions
item.description: What is an authorization decision? Speedle evaluates a subject, action and resource within a service. The application must enforce the result. Treat an evaluation error or timeout separately from a normal Deny and fail closed. REST, gRPC and embedded Go APIs have different wire representations; use their respective contracts. Before running the examples Build ./bin/spctl, ./bin/speedle-pms and ./bin/speedle-ads using the quick start. Use Go 1.26.10 or Go 1.27.3 (or a newer patch on the same release branch), Bash, curl and Python 3.

item.title: Policy Discovery
item.description: What discovery does Discovery records requests and returns allowed=true with reason 5 for a successful recording operation. It does not prove that an existing policy authorized the operation. Use it only in an isolated test environment, review generated grants, and restore normal is-allowed enforcement afterwards. Assertion or storage errors must still be handled; never treat an error as an authorization grant. Start a reproducible local example Build the binaries using Quick Start, then run all terminals from the checkout root.

item.title: Policy Management
item.description: What is a Speedle policy? The Policy Management Service (PMS) manages services, authorization policies, role policies and custom functions. A policy store persists those objects using a registered storage backend. Services and authorization policies A service scopes its policies. An authorization policy grants or denies a principal permission to perform an action on a resource, optionally subject to a condition. Except for global role policies, policies do not automatically apply in another service.

item.title: SPDL - Speedle Policy Definition Language
item.description: Syntax Keywords grant, deny, user, group, entity, role, from, on, if and in have special meanings in their syntax positions. Statement keywords are case-insensitive. In conditions, use in or IN; function names are case-sensitive. Principal, action and resource names are also case-sensitive. The current parser accepts keyword-like names in some name positions, so a blanket prohibition is not a validation rule. Prefer unambiguous names for review and client interoperability.

item.title: Speedle Overview: Authorization Engine for Fine-Grained Access Control
item.description: Speedle is an open-source authorization engine. Applications send it a question such as “may this user perform this action on this resource?”, and Speedle answers allow or deny according to centrally managed policies. This page connects common authorization terms to the Speedle components that implement them, and links to the guides that cover each one. The examples below use a service named library. Each policy was created through the Policy Management Service REST API and each decision was returned by the Authorization Decision Service REST API.
